examples.en: The company is starting its new service today.

examples.ko: 가게가 오전 아홉 시에 영업을 개시했어요.
examples.en: The store began business at nine in the morning.

examples.ko: 공사를 개시하기 전에 주민들에게 알려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to tell the residents before beginning construction.
The government announced that it will begin an investigation.

examples.ko: 은행은 다음 달에 새 대출 상품 판매를 개시할 거예요.
examples.en: The bank will start selling a new loan product next month.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 경기를 개시하자 관중이 환호했어요.
examples.en: When the two teams started the game, the crowd cheered.

explain: '시작하다'보다 딱딱해서 영업, 공사, 조사, 판매 같은 공식적인 일에 주로 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '시작하다'를 써요. 짝말로 '개시하다'의 반대는 '종료하다'예요.

phrases.en: The shop starts business tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개시하다'보다 부드러워서 친구와 이야기할 때도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 개시하다 and natural in casual conversation too.

phrases.en: The restaurant opens for business at ten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 회사가 문을 열고 일을 시작한다는 공식적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal set phrase for a shop or company starting business.

phrases.en: We plan to start the construction next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 시작할 계획을 공지처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an announcement for a planned future start.

explain_en: It is stiffer than 시작하다 and mostly used for formal things like business, construction, investigations and sales. With friends you would say 시작하다. The opposite is 종료하다, to end.

examples.en: The owner hired three employees.
Our shop does not hire students.
I do not have the money to hire anyone yet.
The newly hired employee is very kind.
It can be hard for the side that hires, too.
We are short-handed, so I want to hire a part-timer.

explain: '뽑다'는 지원자 중에서 고르는 것이고, '고용하다'는 뽑은 뒤 일하게 하는 것까지 말해요. 일하는 사람 쪽에서는 '고용되다'라고 해요. 반대말은 '해고하다'예요.

phrases.en: I hired a part-timer and gave them the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 쓴 뒤의 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to continue with what happened after hiring someone.

phrases.en: We will hire more employees next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 미래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a future form for talking about plans.

phrases.en: The company hired that person as a full-time employee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방식으로 쓰는지 '으로'와 함께 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This pairing states the type of employment with '으로'.

explain_en: '뽑다' is choosing from applicants, while '고용하다' includes having the person work afterward. The worker's side uses '고용되다'. The opposite is '해고하다'.

examples.en: The teacher prepared the lesson plan in advance.

examples.ko: 교안을 만드는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Making a lesson plan takes a long time.
The student teacher taught while looking at the lesson plan.
I write the lesson goals and order in the lesson plan.
I'll try teaching the class again with a new lesson plan.
I uploaded the lesson plan to the school website.

explain: 한 학기 전체 계획인 강의계획서와 달리, 교안은 한 번의 수업을 어떻게 진행할지 적은 계획이라는 쪽에 가까워요. 교사나 교생 실습 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '지도안'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I put together the lesson plan for tomorrow's class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업 순서를 생각해서 계획을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means planning the order of a lesson and drafting it.
phrases.en_equiv: to draw up a lesson plan

phrases.en: I wrote a lesson plan and submitted it to the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글로 써서 정리한다는 느낌이 더 있고 조금 격식 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has more of a feel of writing it up formally.

phrases.en: The student teacher showed me the lesson plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교안'과 비슷한 뜻으로, 교생 실습 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning to 'gyoan', often used in student-teaching contexts.

explain_en: Unlike a '강의계획서' (a course-wide plan for a term), a '교안' is closer to a plan for how to run a single lesson. It comes up often in talk about teachers and student teaching, and it is also called '지도안'.

examples.en: The novelist is working out a new story.
I've sketched out my summer vacation plans.
The building the architect conceived will be finished soon.

examples.ko: 사업을 구상할 때는 시장 조사부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: When you plan a business, you should start with market research.

examples.ko: 그림을 그리기 전에 먼저 어떻게 그릴지 구상해요.
examples.en: Before drawing, I first think through how I'll draw it.
It took a whole month to work out the plan.

explain: 글, 그림, 사업, 계획의 큰 틀을 머릿속으로 미리 그릴 때 써요. '생각하다'보다 구체적이고, '계획하다'보다 아직 정해지기 전이에요. 구상한 다음에 계획을 세우고 실행하는 순서예요.

phrases.en: I'm planning out a new novel these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 정해지기 전에 머릿속으로 그리고 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that you are still sketching it in your head before deciding.

phrases.en: I'm working out ideas for the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이디어의 큰 틀을 미리 생각할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when mapping out the main outline of an idea.

phrases.en: I drew the picture as I had planned it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 그려 본 계획대로 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one followed the plan sketched out beforehand.

explain_en: Use it when you picture the broad outline of writing, art, a business, or a plan in your head beforehand. It is more concrete than 생각하다 and earlier than 계획하다. The usual order is 구상 first, then planning, then carrying it out.

dis.h: think up an idea in your head

p.n: 구상하다 is shaping the idea or outline mentally; 계획하다 is deciding concrete steps.

en: to plan; to design; to organize

examples.en: Our team plans a new event.
I planned a trip with a friend.
I work planning exhibitions.
We are looking for someone to plan a new program.
The video I planned is very popular.
After planning the event, I made a poster.

explain: '계획하다'는 앞으로 할 일을 정하는 것이고, '기획하다'는 행사, 상품, 방송처럼 새로운 것을 만들려고 아이디어와 틀을 짜는 것에 가까워요. 직업 이름 '기획자'와 '기획서'를 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I'm planning a family trip for the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기획하다'보다 뜻이 넓어서 개인적인 일에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 기획하다 and works for personal matters too.

phrases.en: I'm currently planning a new program.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 준비하는 중이라는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Progressive form: you are in the middle of planning.

phrases.example: 친구들과 작은 전시를 기획해 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to try planning a small exhibition with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여 한번 해 본다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 보다 gives the feel of trying it out.

explain_en: The general word for planning is about deciding what to do; this one is closer to designing the concept and structure of a new event, product or show. Useful to know with the job title planner and the word for a proposal document.

dis.h: plan and organize a project or event

p.n: 계획하다 is a plain 'plan'; 기획하다 stresses designing and organizing the event itself.

examples.ko: 오늘은 외근 없이 하루 종일 내근이에요.
examples.en: Today I have no outside visits and am in the office all day.

examples.ko: 저는 내근이 많아서 사무실에 거의 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: I do mostly office work, so I'm sitting in the office most of the time.

examples.ko: 내근 직원이 전화를 받아서 전달해 드릴게요.
examples.en: A staff member in the office will take the call and pass it on to you.

examples.ko: 영업팀이지만 이번 주는 내근 위주로 일해요.
examples.en: I'm on the sales team, but this week I'm mostly working in the office.

examples.ko: 내근과 외근 중에서 어느 쪽이 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like better, working in the office or out in the field?

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 외근 대신 내근을 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: It's raining a lot, so we decided to do office work instead of going out.

explain: 반대말은 회사 밖에서 일하는 '외근'이에요. '내근하다', '내근직', '내근 직원'처럼 쓰고, 오늘 일정을 말할 때는 '오늘 내근이에요'라고 간단히 말해요.

phrases.en: I work in the office today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내근'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요. 그날 사무실 안에서 일한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding '하다' to '내근'. Use it to say you work inside the office that day.

phrases.en: An office job is comfortable because there is almost no outside work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사무실 안에서 일하는 직업이나 자리를 말해요. 구직이나 직업 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a job or position that works inside the office. Used in job-hunting and career talk.

phrases.example: 내근 직원이 전화를 받아 드릴 거예요.
phrases.en: An office staff member will take your call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사무실에서 일하는 사람을 가리키는 말이에요. 회사 안내문이나 업무 대화에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people who work in the office. It often appears in company notices and work talk.

explain_en: Its opposite is '외근', working outside the company. It is used in '내근하다', '내근직' and '내근 직원', and for today's schedule people simply say '오늘 내근이에요'.

en: to do something for someone; to do something by proxy

examples.en: The travel agency handles the visa application for you.
The manager acted in place of the boss.
How much is the fee at a company that handles moving for you?

examples.ko: 청소를 대행해 주는 서비스를 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a service that does the cleaning for you.
To act on someone's behalf here, you need permission.

examples.ko: 제가 대행할 수 있는 일은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: There aren't many things I can do on someone's behalf.

explain: 다른 사람이나 회사의 일을 대신 해 줄 때 써요. 서비스 이름에 많아서 '대행사', '대행 수수료'라는 말이 있어요. 친구 일은 보통 '대신 해 주다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아픈 친구 대신 제가 발표를 해 줬어요.
phrases.en: I gave the presentation for my sick friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족 사이에서는 '대행하다'보다 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Among friends and family, use this instead of '대행하다'.

phrases.en: I left the visa application to a travel agency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 다른 곳에 맡기는 사람의 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the view of the person who hands the job over.
phrases.en_equiv: to hand over to an agent

phrases.example: 그 일은 대행사가 모두 해 줘요.
phrases.en: The agency does all of that work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대신 일해 주는 회사를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a company that does work on someone's behalf.

explain_en: Use it when you do someone else's work for them, especially as a service. That is why words like '대행사' and '대행 수수료' exist. For a friend's task, people usually say '대신 해 주다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 취업 준비 때문에 매일 동분서주해요.
examples.en: I'm running around every day these days because of job hunting.
My father ran around everywhere to come up with the kids' tuition.

examples.ko: 사고가 나자 직원들이 동분서주하며 상황을 정리했어요.
examples.en: When the accident happened, the staff scrambled around to sort things out.
It was moving day, so I rushed around all day long.

examples.ko: 저는 전시회를 준비하느라 몇 주째 동분서주하고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been busy running around for weeks preparing for the exhibition.

examples.ko: 그렇게 동분서주했는데도 일이 잘 안 풀려서 속상해요.
examples.en: I ran around so much, yet things didn't work out, and I'm upset.

explain: '바쁘다'는 일이 많은 상태를 말하지만, '동분서주하다'는 이곳저곳을 뛰어다니며 애쓰는 모습을 그려요. 돈을 마련하거나 일을 수습하는 것처럼 목적이 있는 일에 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '이리저리 뛰어다니다'가 더 편하고, '동분서주'는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.example: 아이들 학비를 구하려고 동분서주하며 사람들을 만났어요.
phrases.en: I met many people, running around to get money for the kids' tuition.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동분서주하다'를 다른 동작과 이어서 말할 때 '-며'로 연결해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Link it to another action with '-며' while describing the running around.

phrases.example: 이사 준비로 동분서주하느라 밥도 못 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I was so busy running around for the move that I couldn't even eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바쁘게 뛰어다닌 것이 이유가 되어 다른 일을 못 했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when running around was the reason you couldn't do something else.

phrases.example: 서류를 내려고 하루 종일 이리저리 뛰어다녔어요.
phrases.en: I ran around all day to hand in the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동분서주하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same thing but sounds more casual in speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to run around here and there

explain_en: '바쁘다' describes having a lot to do, while '동분서주하다' paints a picture of rushing from place to place with effort. It fits goal-driven situations such as raising money or sorting out a problem. In speech '이리저리 뛰어다니다' feels more natural, and '동분서주' appears more in writing and news.

en: to close (at a deadline or end of business); to wrap up

examples.en: We close the shop early today.
I have to finish the manuscript by Friday.
Apply before registration closes.

examples.ko: 저녁 여섯 시에 은행이 업무를 마감했어요.
examples.en: The bank closed for business at six in the evening.
We ended the season with good results this year.
After it's closed, you can't edit it.

explain: 정해진 시간이나 기한이 되어 일을 끝내고 문을 닫는 걸 말해요. 명사 '마감'은 '마감 날짜', '마감 시간'처럼 일상에서 아주 많이 써요. '끝내다'보다 기한이 정해져 있다는 느낌이 강하고, '마감 임박'은 곧 끝난다는 광고 문구예요.

phrases.en: The shop's closing time is nine o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '마감'에 '시간'을 붙여서 일상에서 아주 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '마감' plus '시간' is very common in daily life.

phrases.en: Applications closed yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 일이나 신청이 주어일 때는 '마감되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '마감되다' when the subject is the thing, such as applications, rather than a person.

phrases.en: I'll finish today's work and go home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마감하다'보다 쉬운 말이지만 기한의 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '마감하다', but with less of a deadline feel.

explain_en: Wrapping up work and closing at a set time or deadline. The noun '마감' is very common: '마감 날짜', '마감 시간'. It stresses a fixed deadline more than '끝내다' does, and '마감 임박' is an ad phrase meaning 'closing soon'.

dis.h: close for the day or at a deadline

p.n: 마감하다 is the formal closing of business or a deadline; 끝내다 is just ending.

en: to be responsible; to be in charge

examples.en: I'll take charge of preparing for this event.
My older brother is in charge of the shop's work.
Who is in charge of the accounting work?

examples.ko: 그는 오래전부터 동네 반장 일을 맡아봤어요.
examples.en: He has handled the neighborhood leader's work for a long time.

examples.ko: 내가 대신 아이들을 맡아볼 테니 다녀와요.
examples.en: I'll look after the kids for you, so go ahead.
The person in charge of general affairs sends out the messages.

explain: '맡다'와 거의 같지만 어떤 일을 맡아서 계속 처리하고 관리한다는 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '맡다'가 더 많이 쓰이고, '맡아보다'는 조금 더 책임지고 돌보는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 동생이 우리 가게 장부를 맡아보고 있어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is in charge of our shop's books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 계속 책임지고 처리하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is continuing to take responsibility for a task.

phrases.example: 이 일은 민수 씨가 한번 맡아보세요.
phrases.en: Minsu, why don't you take charge of this job?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 어떤 일을 책임져 달라고 부드럽게 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to ask someone to take responsibility for a task.

phrases.en: We're looking for someone to take charge of the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 책임질 사람을 구할 때 쓰는 꾸밈 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used when looking for someone to take responsibility.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '맡다', but with the feeling of taking on a task and handling and managing it continuously. In daily talk '맡다' is more common, while '맡아보다' feels a bit more like taking responsibility.

examples.en: The publisher puts out a new magazine every year.
The school decided to publish a graduation collection.

examples.ko: 연구소가 보고서를 발간하고 나서 기자회견을 열었어요.
examples.en: The institute published its report and then held a press conference.

examples.ko: 이번 달 안에 보고서를 발간하려고 열심히 준비 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm working hard to publish the report within this month.

examples.ko: 한 권을 발간하는 데 몇 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took several months to publish one volume.

examples.ko: 그 신문은 백 년 전부터 계속 발간해 왔어요.
examples.en: That newspaper has been published continuously for a hundred years.

explain: 책 한 권을 내는 일은 '출간하다'나 '출판하다'를 많이 쓰고, '발간하다'는 잡지·신문·보고서처럼 정해진 때에 계속 내는 인쇄물에 잘 어울려요. 신문과 화폐에는 '발행하다'도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 작가는 올해 새 책을 출간했어요.
phrases.en: That author published a new book this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 한 권을 낼 때는 '발간하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more than 발간하다 for putting out a single book.

phrases.en: The newspaper company publishes a paper every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문이나 화폐처럼 찍어서 내놓는 것에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for printing and issuing newspapers or currency.

phrases.en: The report will be published next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발간하다'의 피동형으로, 인쇄물이 나오는 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the publication coming out.

explain_en: For bringing out a single book, 출간하다 or 출판하다 is common. 발간하다 suits periodic printed matter such as magazines, newspapers and reports. 발행하다 is also used for newspapers and currency.

p.n: 간행 is more formal and bookish than 발간.

examples.en: The teacher assigned the students to classes.
I'll assign your room first.
We are dividing and assigning the work to each person.
It takes time to assign the seats.
We will allot the budget to each department.
We haven't assigned a person in charge yet.

explain: 'A를 B에 배정하다'처럼 누구를 어디에 정해 줄 때 써요. 정해 주는 사람이 주어이고, 정해진 사람이 주어이면 '배정되다'를 써요. 단순히 일을 시킬 때는 '맡기다'가 더 편해요.

phrases.en: Please assign me to the morning class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배정하다'에 부탁하는 말투를 붙인 표현이라 직접 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This adds a polite request to the verb, so you use it when asking someone directly.

phrases.en: I was assigned to class 3.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 사람이 주어일 때는 '배정하다' 대신 '배정되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When the person who gets placed is the subject, use 배정되다 instead of 배정하다.

phrases.en: The teacher assigned seats to the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리, 방, 반처럼 장소를 정해 줄 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for assigning a place such as a seat, a room, or a class.

explain_en: It is used in 'A를 B에 배정하다' when someone decides where someone or something goes. The person deciding is the subject; if the assigned person is the subject, use 배정되다. For simply handing someone a job, 맡기다 is easier.

examples.en: He works as an aide to the president.
Assisting the president is very busy work.
I took on the role of assistant to the team leader.

examples.ko: 의원 보좌 일을 하면서 정치를 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about politics while working as an aide to a lawmaker.

examples.ko: 좋은 보좌가 있으면 일이 훨씬 쉬워져요.
examples.en: With a good aide, work becomes much easier.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 오랫동안 시장의 보좌를 했어요.
examples.en: He served as the mayor's aide for a long time.

explain: 윗사람이나 중요한 사람 곁에서 일을 돕는 것이에요. 그냥 '도움'이나 '돕기'와 달리 높은 자리를 돕는다는 느낌이 있어요. 회사에서는 '비서'나 '보조'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: He is an aide to a member of the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 자리에 있는 사람을 돕는 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a job that helps someone in a high position.

phrases.en: The CEO works with the help of a secretary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 사람의 입장에서 도움을 받는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the senior person who receives help.

phrases.en: I took on the role of assisting the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람 곁에서 돕는 일을 '역할'과 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the role of helping a superior.

explain_en: Helping a superior or an important person from close by. Unlike plain 도움, it implies assisting someone in a high position. In companies 비서 or 보조 is more common.

examples.en: My parental leave is over, so I return to work next week.

examples.ko: 선배는 병이 나은 뒤에 회사로 복직했어요.
examples.en: My senior returned to the company after recovering.

examples.ko: 복직하면 예전 부서로 돌아갈 수 있나요?
examples.en: When I return to work, can I go back to my old department?
My sister plans to return to work next year.
On the first day back at work, everything felt unfamiliar.

examples.ko: 복직하기 전에 인사팀에 서류를 내야 해요.
examples.en: Before returning to work, you have to submit documents to HR.

explain: '복직하다'는 쉬었거나 일을 그만둔 사람이 원래 직장으로 돌아오는 거예요. 휴직 뒤에 쓰는 말이고, 새 회사에 들어가는 건 '취직하다'나 '입사하다'라고 해요. 쉬는 건 '휴직', 돌아오는 건 '복직'으로 짝을 이뤄요.

phrases.en: I'm going to return to work next March.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴직 뒤에 돌아올 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a plan to return after leave.

phrases.en: I recovered from my illness and applied to return to the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복직'은 명사로 신청이나 허락과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun, '복직' goes with applying or being approved.

phrases.example: 휴가가 끝나서 다음 주에 회사에 복귀해요.
phrases.en: My leave is over, so I'm going back to the company next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복직'보다 넓게, 휴가 뒤에 일터로 돌아올 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than '복직'; it also works for coming back to work after a short leave.

explain_en: 복직하다 means going back to your original workplace after time off or leaving. It is paired with 휴직 (taking leave). Joining a new company is 취직하다 or 입사하다 instead.

examples.en: The company steps up its overseas expansion from this year.
The government decided to start the support program in earnest.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 다음 달에 활동을 본격화할 거예요.
examples.en: That singer will begin full-scale activities next month.
Our team has now gotten serious about preparations.
At the stage of going full-scale, we need more people.

examples.ko: 연구를 본격화해서 내년에 결과를 낼 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to move the research into full gear and produce results next year.

explain: 사람이나 단체가 어떤 일을 제대로, 힘을 들여 시작할 때 써요. '활동을 본격화하다'처럼 목적어를 받아요. 일이 저절로 그렇게 되면 '본격화되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The company went into full swing on developing the new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형이에요. 사람이나 단체가 제대로 시작했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, meaning a person or group got started in earnest.

phrases.example: 학교는 올해부터 안전 교육을 본격화하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The school decided to start safety education in earnest from this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 결정을 말할 때 '-기로 하다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-기로 하다' when talking about plans or decisions.

phrases.en: I start preparing for the exam in earnest from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻을 더 쉽게 풀어 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to express the same idea.

explain_en: Use it when a person or group starts doing something properly and with real effort. It takes an object, as in '활동을 본격화하다'. When things simply develop that way on their own, use '본격화되다'.

examples.en: After work, I do translation at home as a side job.
My salary alone wasn't enough, so I started a side job.

examples.ko: 부업 때문에 요즘 잠을 많이 못 자요.
examples.en: Because of my side job, I can't get much sleep these days.
At my company, it's fine to have a side job.
The side job I do every weekend is harder than I thought.

examples.ko: 어떤 부업이 나에게 맞을지 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into which side job would suit me.

explain: 짝말은 '본업'이에요. '부업을 하다', '부업을 시작하다'처럼 쓰고, 요즘은 같은 뜻으로 '투잡'이라는 말도 많이 해요. 부업은 돈을 버는 일에 쓰고, 취미에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: These days many people have two jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부업'과 비슷한 말인데 더 가볍고 구어적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 부업 but more casual and colloquial.

phrases.en: I work at a cafe on weekends as a side job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 부업임을 밝힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that a job is a side job.
phrases.en_equiv: to do as a side job

phrases.example: 본업과 부업을 같이 하니까 많이 피곤해요.
phrases.en: Doing both my main job and side job makes me very tired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '본업'과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite, 본업 (main job).

explain_en: The opposite is 본업, the main job. You say '부업을 하다' or '부업을 시작하다', and these days people also say '투잡' for the same idea. 부업 is for work that earns money, not for hobbies.

examples.ko: 새 교장 선생님이 오늘 학교에 부임하셨어요.
examples.en: The new principal took up the post at the school today.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 부산 지사로 부임할 예정이에요.
examples.en: I'm scheduled to take up a post at the Busan branch next month.
On my first day in the new post, I greeted the staff.

examples.ko: 새 선생님은 부임하자마자 학교 문제를 하나씩 해결했어요.
examples.en: As soon as the new teacher took up the post, the school's problems were solved one by one.

examples.ko: 시골 학교에 부임해서 아이들과 즐겁게 지내요.
examples.en: I took a post at a rural school and am enjoying time with the children.
Before taking up the post, I found a place to move to.

explain: '부임하다'는 새 직장이나 임지에 가서 일을 시작할 때 써요. 학교의 교장, 대사, 지사장처럼 직책이 있는 사람에게 잘 어울려요. 일반 회사에 새로 들어가는 건 '입사하다'가 자연스러워요. 높임은 '부임하시다'예요.

phrases.en: The new ambassador will take up the post next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높여야 하는 사람이 새 자리에 갈 때 쓰는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for a respected person taking up a new post.

phrases.en: The newly appointed principal is kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 지금 막 온 사람을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to introduce someone who has just arrived at a post.

phrases.example: 제 첫 부임지는 작은 시골 학교였어요.
phrases.en: My first posting was a small rural school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 일하러 간 곳을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the first place one was assigned to work.

explain_en: 부임하다 is used when someone goes to a new workplace or posting and starts work. It suits people with a position, like a school principal, an ambassador, or a branch head. For joining an ordinary company, 입사하다 is more natural. The honorific is 부임하시다.

examples.ko: 회사가 다음 달에 새 사옥으로 이사해요.
examples.en: The company moves to a new building next month.

examples.ko: 그 회사 사옥은 강남역 근처에 있어요.
examples.en: That company's headquarters building is near Gangnam Station.
I waited for a guest in the building lobby.

examples.ko: 큰 사옥을 짓는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to build the large office building.
People are gathered in front of the company building.
Our company building has a cafe and a gym.

explain: 사옥은 회사가 통째로 쓰는 건물이에요. 큰 건물 안의 한 층만 쓰면 '사무실'이라고 하고, 사옥은 회사 이름이 붙은 건물을 말할 때 써요. 회사 소식에서 '본사 사옥'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the head office building tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사의 중심이 되는 건물을 말할 때 쓰는 합친 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound used for the main building of a company.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 서울에 새 사옥을 지었어요.
phrases.en: That company built a new office building in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 새로 만든다는 뜻으로 '짓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 짓다 to mean constructing a new building.

phrases.example: 사옥 이전 때문에 이번 주가 바빠요.
phrases.en: This week is busy because of the office building move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 건물을 다른 곳으로 옮기는 일을 한 덩어리로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the move of a company to another building as a single idea.

explain_en: 사옥 is a building a company uses as a whole. If a company has only one floor in a larger building, it is a 사무실 (office). 사옥 is for a building carrying the company's name; '본사 사옥' (headquarters building) is common in company news.

examples.en: I handed in my resignation letter this morning.
It was really hard to submit my resignation to my manager.
You have to write the leaving date on the resignation letter.
I wonder why you suddenly wrote a resignation letter.
My resignation letter has not been accepted yet.

examples.ko: 사직서를 내기 전에 한 번 더 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Think once more before you hand in your resignation.

explain: 사직서는 회사를 그만두겠다고 알리는 서류이고, 보통 '사직서를 내다, 쓰다, 제출하다'로 말해요. 그만두는 일은 '퇴사'나 '퇴직'이라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '그만두다'를 더 많이 써요. 회사가 내보내는 '해고'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I handed in my resignation letter to the company yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사직서를 회사에 건네는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the act of handing the letter to the company.
phrases.en_equiv: to hand in a resignation letter

phrases.en: After worrying all night, I wrote my resignation letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 직접 작성하는 단계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the step of actually writing the document.

phrases.en: The boss received an employee's resignation letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 쪽에서 사직서를 받는 입장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Speaks from the company's side as the one receiving the letter.

explain_en: 사직서 is the document announcing that you will leave a job, used as 사직서를 내다, 쓰다 or 제출하다. The act of leaving is 퇴사 or 퇴직, but in daily talk 그만두다 is more common. It differs from 해고, where the company dismisses you.

examples.en: A doctor is on duty at this hospital around the clock.
A manager is stationed in the building, so I feel safe.
The research team is made up of people who live permanently at the Antarctic base.
A building with no guard on site feels unsafe.

examples.ko: 공사 기간에 직원 두 명이 현장에 상주했어요.
examples.en: Two staff members stayed on the site during construction.

examples.ko: 도우미가 상주할 수 있는 방이 필요해요.
examples.en: I need a room where a helper can live.

explain: '살다'는 집이 있는 사람에게 쓰고, '상주하다'는 일하는 사람이 어떤 곳에 계속 머물러 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 안내문에 '직원 상주'라고 많이 보여요. 장례식의 '상주'(주 되는 가족)와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: There is a resident staff member in the building, so I feel safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 자주 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun collocation common on notices.

phrases.en: There is no resident doctor on this island.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상주하는'을 명사 앞에 붙여 계속 머무는 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier 상주하는 describes a person who stays there all the time.

phrases.en: A nurse is staying in the hospital room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이에요. 일하는 사람이라는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word, without the sense of working on-site.

explain_en: '살다' is for where a person lives, while '상주하다' means a person who works there stays on site all the time. Signs often say '직원 상주' (staff on site). It is a different word from '상주', the chief mourner at a funeral.

en: to design; to plan out (a structure or system)

examples.en: An architect designed the new library.
We need to design the app again from scratch.

examples.ko: 집을 설계할 때 햇빛을 가장 먼저 생각했어요.
examples.en: When designing the house, I thought about sunlight first.
Take time to plan your future.

examples.ko: 튼튼하게 설계하면 오래 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you design it sturdily, you can use it for a long time.
My younger sibling is designing a robot by himself.

explain: 건물, 기계, 시스템의 구조를 미리 그림이나 계획으로 짜는 일이에요. 겉모양을 꾸미는 '디자인하다'와 달리 구조와 방식을 정하는 쪽이에요. '인생을 설계하다'처럼 계획을 크게 세울 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 이 집은 유명한 건축가가 설계한 집이에요.
phrases.en: This house was designed by a famous architect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I tried planning out my life in my twenties.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생처럼 큰 계획을 세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a large-scale plan, such as for one's life.

phrases.en: We build the house by looking at the blueprint.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설계한 내용을 그린 그림을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the drawing that shows the design.

explain_en: This is planning the structure of a building, machine, or system in advance with drawings or a blueprint. Unlike 디자인하다, which is about appearance, it is about structure and method. It also works for big plans, like 인생을 설계하다.

en: to take the initiative and set an example

examples.en: Only when the executives set an example first will the staff follow.
The team leader sets an example even when cleaning.
If seniors lead by example, juniors follow well.
As a parent, I try to lead by example too.
He is respected for always leading by example.
I wish the people who made the rules would set an example.

explain: '솔선하다'가 먼저 나서는 행동에 초점이 있다면, '솔선수범하다'는 남들이 본받을 모범이 되는 데 초점이 있어요. 주로 윗사람이나 책임 있는 사람에게 기대할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 솔선수범하는 선배 덕분에 후배들이 잘 따라요.
phrases.en: Thanks to a senior who sets an example, the juniors follow well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸미는 활용형으로, 좋은 선배나 리더를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used to describe a good senior or leader.

phrases.en: Please, adults, set an example first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 정중하게 부탁하거나 요구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely request that people in charge set an example.

phrases.en: The boss set an example in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자어를 쓰지 않고 쉽게 말하는 같은 뜻의 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing without the Sino-Korean word.

explain_en: While '솔선하다' focuses on stepping forward first, '솔선수범하다' focuses on becoming a model for others to follow. It is mostly used when expecting this of superiors or people with responsibility.

examples.ko: 숙직 다음 날은 반차를 쓸 수 있도록 배려해 줘요.
examples.en: They let you take a half-day off the day after night duty.

examples.ko: 아버지는 젊었을 때 학교에서 숙직을 서신 적이 있다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My father said he once did night duty at a school when he was young.
Today I'm on night duty at the office.

examples.ko: 병원에서 숙직하는 의사들은 거의 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: Doctors who do night duty at the hospital hardly sleep.

examples.ko: 어제 숙직하느라 피곤해서 오늘 일찍 퇴근했어요.
examples.en: I was tired from night duty yesterday, so I left work early today.

examples.ko: 숙직할 사람을 정해야 하는데 누가 할래요?
examples.en: We need to decide who will take night duty. Who wants to?

explain: 밤에 회사나 학교, 관공서를 지키는 일을 말하고, '숙직을 서다'라고도 자연스럽게 해요. 낮에 맡는 당번은 '일직'이라고 하고, 밤낮 구분 없이는 '당직'을 써요.

phrases.en: Tonight I'm on night duty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙직하다'를 자연스럽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrasing of '숙직하다'.

phrases.en: I rested for a while in the night duty room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숙직하는 사람이 쉬거나 자는 방이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room where the person on night duty rests or sleeps.

phrases.en: I'm on duty at the hospital on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밤낮 구분 없이 맡는 당번에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for duty not limited to night or day.

explain_en: It means staying overnight to look after a company, school or government office, and '숙직을 서다' is also natural. Daytime duty is '일직', and '당직' is the general word for being on duty.

examples.ko: 대통령은 이번 주에 지방 순회를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The president began a tour of the provinces this week.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 순회 공연이 다음 달에 시작돼요.
examples.en: That singer's touring concerts start next month.

examples.ko: 긴 순회 공연이 끝나고 가수는 오랜만에 집에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: After the long tour, the singer came home for the first time in a while.
The guard makes rounds of the building every night.

examples.ko: 이번 순회에 참가한 학생이 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: Ten students in all took part in this tour.

examples.ko: 경비 순회는 하루에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: The guard's rounds happen twice a day.

explain: '돌아다니다'는 목적 없이도 쓰지만 '순회'는 정해진 곳을 차례로 돌며 일을 하는 거예요. '순회 공연', '지방 순회', '순회 진료'처럼 다른 명사 앞에도 붙어요. 일상 대화보다 안내문이나 뉴스에서 봐요.

phrases.example: 그 가수가 전국 순회 공연을 해요.
phrases.en: That singer is doing a nationwide tour of concerts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 지역을 차례로 돌며 하는 공연을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for performances held in several places one after another.

phrases.en: Doctors give mobile medical care in island villages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에 오기 어려운 곳을 찾아다니며 진료하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doctors travel to places where people can't easily reach a hospital.

phrases.en: The president is now touring the provinces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 곳을 차례로 돌고 있는 중이라는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is in the middle of going round set places; often heard in the news.

explain_en: 돌아다니다 can be aimless, but 순회 means going through set places in order to do a job. It also sits in front of other nouns, as in '순회 공연', '지방 순회', and '순회 진료'. You meet it in notices and news more than in conversation.

examples.en: There's no rush, so take it easy and do it bit by bit.
If you hike up with rests along the way, it isn't tiring.
My grandfather does the field work at a relaxed pace, resting often.

examples.ko: 쉬엄쉬엄 걸었더니 두 시간이 훌쩍 지났어요.
examples.en: We walked with plenty of breaks, and two hours flew by.

examples.ko: 일이 많아도 쉬엄쉬엄 해야 오래 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even when there's a lot of work, you have to pace yourself to keep going for long.
On the weekend, I cleaned at a relaxed pace and watched a movie.

explain: '천천히'가 속도를 말한다면, '쉬엄쉬엄'은 중간중간 쉬어 가면서 한다는 느낌이에요. '쉬엄쉬엄 하세요'는 무리하지 말라고 상대를 챙기는 말로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I walked along the mountain trail, resting now and then.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걷다가 중간중간 쉬는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes walking while resting here and there.

phrases.en: It's not urgent, so take it easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무리하지 말라고 상대를 챙길 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to look out for someone, telling them not to overdo it.

phrases.en: Study slowly, taking breaks as you go.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쉬엄쉬엄'과 비슷한 뜻으로 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way of saying something close to 쉬엄쉬엄.

explain_en: While '천천히' is about speed, '쉬엄쉬엄' feels like doing something while taking breaks in between. '쉬엄쉬엄 하세요' is also commonly said to tell someone not to overdo it.

examples.ko: 시험 시간을 잘 안배해서 문제를 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to allocate the exam time well to solve the questions.
I climbed the mountain slowly, pacing my strength.
The committee selected people, balancing them by region.
If you budget your salary, you have a bit of money left.

examples.ko: 일을 안배하지 못해서 마감 직전에 야근했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't plan my work well, so I worked overtime right before the deadline.
The coach distributed the players' playing time.

explain: 시간, 체력, 인원, 예산처럼 한정된 것을 형편에 맞게 알맞게 나누어 짜 놓을 때 써요. 무엇을 안배하는지 목적어를 꼭 같이 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '나눠서 쓰다', '조절하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Try planning out your time before the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한정된 시간을 나누어 계획한다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning to plan out limited time.

phrases.en: On a long trip, you need to pace your energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 한꺼번에 쓰지 않고 나누어 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means spreading out your energy instead of using it all at once.

phrases.example: 예산을 잘 안배해서 한 달을 살았어요.
phrases.en: I allocated my budget well and lived through the month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해서'로 이어서 이유나 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '-haeseo' to state a reason or method.

explain_en: Use it when you divide and arrange limited things such as time, energy, people or budget appropriately for the situation. You always say what is being allocated as the object. In everyday talk people also say '나눠서 쓰다' or '조절하다'.

examples.en: The teacher taught the students with great dedication.

examples.ko: 모두 열성껏 준비한 덕분에 행사가 잘 끝났어요.
examples.en: Because everyone prepared with such dedication, the event went well.
Thank you so much for helping so wholeheartedly.
Many parents raise their children with great dedication.
We cheered with all our hearts, but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원이 열성껏 일해서 칭찬을 받았어요.
examples.en: The new employee worked with enthusiasm and got praised.

explain: '열심히'는 어떤 일에든 쓰지만, '열성껏'은 마음과 정성을 다한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 가르치기, 돕기, 응원하기처럼 남을 위한 일과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I study Korean hard every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에든 쓸 수 있는 가장 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most general word, usable with almost any activity.

phrases.en: I prepared the food with care for the guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: '열성껏'처럼 마음을 담는 느낌이지만, 만들기나 준비하기에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 열성껏 it carries heart, but fits making and preparing better.

phrases.en: The neighbors helped with the move wholeheartedly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 돕는 일과 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for helping others.

explain_en: '열심히' fits almost any task, while '열성껏' carries a stronger sense of putting heart and effort into it. It suits things done for others, such as teaching, helping and cheering.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 안에 새 공장을 완공하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to complete the new factory within this year.
The contractor finished the building ahead of schedule.

examples.ko: 다리를 완공하는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to complete the bridge.

examples.ko: 건설사는 겨울이 오기 전에 도로를 완공할 거예요.
examples.en: The construction company will finish the road before winter.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 완공한 건물이 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The building our team completed won an award.

examples.ko: 건물을 빨리 완공하고 싶어도 날씨가 도와주지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if we want to finish the building quickly, the weather won't cooperate.

explain: 완공하다는 짓는 회사나 사람이 주어예요. 건물이 주어이면 '완공되다'를 써요. 공사 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '다 지었어요'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.en: The construction company finished building the apartment complex.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '완공하다'보다 '다 짓다'가 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 다 짓다 is easier than 완공하다.

phrases.en: The company finished the construction on the promised date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 쪽이 주어일 때 자연스럽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural when the party doing the work is the subject.

phrases.en: The city announced that it had completed the new park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사 뉴스나 안내에서 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage common in construction news and notices.

explain_en: 완공하다 has the builder (a company or person) as its subject; when the building itself is the subject, use 완공되다. You see it in construction news and notices, while everyday speech more often says 다 지었어요 (we finished building it).

en: to entrust; to leave in another person's hands

examples.en: The chairman left all decisions in the CEO's hands.

examples.ko: 저는 여행 계획을 친구에게 일임하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to leave the travel plans entirely to my friend.

examples.ko: 이 일은 전문가에게 일임하면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: If you leave this job to an expert, you can relax.
I'd like you to leave the decision completely to me.
After entrusting something to someone, I try not to interfere.
I'll leave the choice of menu entirely up to you.

explain: '맡기다'보다 딱딱하고, 판단과 결정까지 통째로 맡긴다는 느낌이 강해요. '~에게 ~을 일임하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '다 맡길게요'라고도 해요. '위임하다'는 권한을 넘기는 쪽에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: I'll leave all the trip preparations to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일임하다'보다 훨씬 부드러운 일상 말이라서 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much softer everyday word than '일임하다', widely used in conversation.

phrases.en: Please leave this matter entirely to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결정까지 모두 맡겨 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request to be given full responsibility, including the decisions.

phrases.en: The running of the company was entrusted entirely to him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일임하다'의 피동 표현이라서, 통째로 맡겨진 일을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive of '일임하다', used when the thing entrusted is the subject.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '맡기다' and strongly suggests handing over the judgment and decision completely. It is used as '~에게 ~을 일임하다', and in daily talk people also say '다 맡길게요'. '위임하다' is closer to handing over authority.

examples.en: I volunteered to give the presentation first.
He took on the hard job of his own accord.
Nobody volunteered to be team leader.
My brother offered to do the dishes, so I just left it to him.

examples.ko: 내가 자청하고 나선 일이니 끝까지 해야죠.
examples.en: I stepped up for this myself, so I have to see it through.

examples.ko: 청소를 자청한 친구 덕분에 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the friend who volunteered to clean, it finished quickly.

explain: 남이 시키기 전에 스스로 나서서 맡는다는 점에서 '자원하다'와 비슷해요. 힘들거나 책임이 따르는 일에 특히 잘 어울리고, '발표를 자청하다', '자청해서 하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He volunteered to take on the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자청해서 + 동사' 형태로 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used in the form '자청해서 + verb'.

phrases.en: I signed up of my own will for the community service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말인데, 자원하다는 하고 싶어서 신청한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but 자원하다 feels more like signing up because you want to.

phrases.en: I volunteered for it, so I can't complain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 나서서 맡은 일을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a task one took on of one's own accord.

explain_en: It is similar to '자원하다' in that you step forward on your own before anyone asks. It suits tasks that are hard or carry responsibility, as in '발표를 자청하다' or '자청해서 하다'.
